prompts.display_text: Pin Nauvoo, Illinois, where the trek west began in 1846.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on Nauvoo, Illinois, the Mississippi River city the Saints began leaving in February 1846 to start the trek west.
prompts.citation: Church History Topics, Nauvoo (Commerce), Illinois; Historic Nauvoo North Visitors' Center page, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The Saints built Nauvoo on land along the Mississippi River that included the small town of Commerce. After finishing the temple, where thousands received the endowment, they began leaving the city in February 1846. The temple was later destroyed, and the Church completed a rebuilt Nauvoo Temple in 2002.

prompts.summary: French is an official language in countries on four continents that have temples, from Canada and Switzerland to Haiti, Vanuatu and much of Africa. Paris, Bern, Port-au-Prince, Kinshasa and Abidjan are dedicated. Brussels, Brazzaville, Antananarivo and Port Vila are under construction as of November 2026.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where people were baptized on its soil while Joseph Smith was still alive.
prompts.text_original: A country where converts were baptized on its own soil before the death of Joseph Smith on June 27, 1844.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: By the time Joseph Smith was killed in June 1844, the Church had spread beyond the United States. Converts had been baptized in Canada, the British Isles and Australia, and on Tubuai in French Polynesia just days before the martyrdom.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: In 1837 George Watt and eight others, the first converts in England, were baptized in the River Ribble at Preston; Scotland, Wales and Ireland (at Loughbrickland, now Northern Ireland) followed by 1843.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Joseph Smith organized the restored Church on April 6, 1830.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: In 1836 Parley P. Pratt baptized a group near Toronto that included John and Leonora Taylor and the Fieldings.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: In 1842 William Barratt baptized Robert Beauchamp Dolling in Adelaide, the first known baptism in Australia.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: On June 16, 1844, Ambrose Alexander became the first convert in French Polynesia, baptized on Tubuai.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose earliest members joined the Church far from home, baptized abroad before any baptism there.
prompts.text_original: A country whose earliest known converts were baptized in another country before anyone was baptized in their homeland.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Some lands had members before missionaries ever baptized anyone there. English emigrants joined in Canada, Danes and an Italian in Boston, Norwegians near Nauvoo, a Netherlander in Wales, a Belgian in France, a Spaniard in Utah and a Bulgarian in Romania. Several later carried the gospel home.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Peter Clemensen and Hans Christian Hansen, the first Danish converts, were baptized in Boston in 1842; the first baptisms in Denmark came in 1850.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: In 1836 Joseph Fielding, John Taylor, Leonora Cannon Taylor and other English immigrants joined the Church in Toronto, a year before the first baptisms in England.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Joseph Toronto (Giuseppe Taranto), the first known Italian convert, was baptized in Boston in 1843; the first baptism in Italy came in 1850.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: Several Norwegians living near Nauvoo joined the Church in the 1840s, before the first baptisms in Norway in 1851.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Gustave Choprix, a Belgian convert baptized in France, preached in Brussels in 1861; the first baptisms in Belgium came in 1888.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Meliton Gonzalez Trejo, a native of Spain, was baptized in Salt Lake City in 1874; resident Spaniards were first baptized only in 1950.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Anne Wiegers van der Woude, the first Netherlander baptized, joined in Cardiff, Wales, in 1852; van der Woude was among the first missionaries to preach in the Netherlands in 1861.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Argir Dimitrov, a Bulgarian working in Turkey, was baptized by Mischa Markow at Constanta, Romania, in 1899.
